title: urgent: stabilize per-model priming oscillations through resilient microbatch handshake and hedged warmup
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported intermittent first-token latency spikes and reduced tokens/sec during priming-heavy workloads after last runtime rollout. Symptom profile: repeated 200–900ms TTFT spikes for short sessions (<=50 tokens) and sustained tokens/sec drop by ~25% under mixed prompt-length workloads. Observed higher failure rate for sessions that arrive concurrently with model-variant probing and background KV prefetch tasks.

Investigation highlights:
- Reproduced in staging using a synthetic fanout workload with small context windows and frequent model-variant checks.
- Telemetry showed microbatch handshake races between coalescer and worker when warmup/priming I/O coincided with variant probe traffic.
- Root cause: race in microbatch handshake state machine that allowed inflight priming requests to block worker availability briefly; compounded by per-model warmup hedging policy that retriggered priming on perception of slow warmup, causing oscillation.

Proposed immediate fix (hotfix path):
1) Harden microbatch handshake: add idempotent handshake ACK path and short-circuit duplicate handshakes for same worker/batch id.
2) Add transient suppression window for hedged warmup triggers (200ms) to prevent re-probing during observed jitter windows.
3) Conservative default: reduce concurrent variant-probe parallelism from 3 to 1 for short-session routing on hosted/dedicated; make configurable for Private.

Rollout plan:
- Stage Canary: deploy patch to staging and run synthetic fanout test for 6 hours; target TTFT median improvement >=20% and tokens/sec within 90% of baseline.
- Beta: rollback-safe canary to 5% of Hosted and Dedicated traffic (non-enterprise) for 2h, monitor dashboards.
- Ramp: 25% -> 75% -> 100% across Hosted/Dedicated over 24h with auto-rollback on SLO breach. Private: publish patch and recommended config, coordinate with three active Private customers for on-prem scheduling.

Monitoring and validation:
- Dashboards: first_byte_latency, ttft_p50/p95, tokens_per_second per model and per-deployment.
- New telemetry: handshake_duplicate_count, hedged_warmup_suppressions.
- Alert thresholds: p95 TTFT increase >30% or tokens/sec drop >20% for >15m triggers rollback.

Customer comms and remediation:
- Notified affected customers with short remediation note and ETA for hotfix.
- Prepared mitigation runbook for support: temporary knob to disable hedged warmup and lower probe parallelism per-customer.

Longer-term follow-ups:
- Replace heuristic hedged-warmup with confidence-model that uses recent per-worker warmup latency distribution.
- Add formal verification tests for microbatch handshake state transitions.

Links: see links field for PRs, dashboards, and runbooks.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Triage: Received customer escalation from three accounts; assigned to Diego. Initial hypothesis: warmup/priming interaction. Added to Latency & Reliability project.
2025-02-11 - Diego: Reproduced a 28% drop in tokens/sec in staging with modeled fanout; collected pprof and handshake traces. Noted duplicate handshake attempts from coalescer under burst traffic.

2025-02-12 - Engineering sync: Agreed hotfix components: (1) idempotent handshake ACK, (2) hedged-warmup suppression window, (3) reduce probe parallelism for short sessions. Diego to implement patch, Priya to own telemetry and alert updates.
2025-02-13 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289 - includes handshake guard and suppression flag. Added feature flag 'suppress_hedged_warmup_ms'.

2025-02-14 - QA: Ran synthetic fanout in staging for 4h, median TTFT improved 18%, tokens/sec at 93% of baseline; observed handshake_duplicate_count drop to near-zero. One regression detected: slight increase in cold-start median for very long contexts; tracked as follow-up (ENG-763001).
2025-02-15 - Canary deploy: 5% hosted traffic. Monitoring: p95 TTFT down by 22%, tokens/sec stable. No customer-facing errors. Proceeding to ramp.

2025-02-17 - Ramp to 75% deployed. One enterprise Dedicated account reported a transient 10% throughput dip correlated with an unrelated autoscaler event; not tied to this change. Notified SRE and paused further ramp until issue resolved.

2025-02-18 - Action: Disabled probe parallelism reduction for Private clusters until coordination call with on-prem operators. Patch remains on Hosted/Dedicated. Diego asked for additional telemetry to capture per-worker warmup histograms. Added to follow-ups.

Follow-ups: create ENG-763001 for long-context cold-start median regression analysis; create ENG-763002 to implement confidence-based warmup model; document runbook knob for Private customers to tune hedged-warmup suppression.
